## My request for Codex:
how can i push my current project to git with Tag version 1.0.0

To publish your current state with a 1.0.0 tag, run these commands from `c:\Users\viritpol.k\Desktop\rpa_test_work_lab\RPA\RPA-DB_market_dashboard\sale website\L4KDev` (replace placeholders in angle brackets):

```
git init                     # only if the repo isn’t initialized yet
git add -A                   # stage all tracked/untracked changes
git commit -m "Release 1.0.0"
git remote add origin <https://github.com/you/your-repo.git>   # skip if already configured
git push -u origin main      # or whichever branch you’re using
git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "Release 1.0.0"
git push origin v1.0.0
```

Notes:
- If the branch already exists remotely, drop `-u` and just `git push origin <branch>`.
- Use a different tag name if `v1.0.0` is already taken; tags must be unique per repo.

## My request for Codex:
v.1.0.0 smoke test 
for another run my project can specific version right ?

If you want to do a quick smoke test of the code you just tagged v1.0.0:

1. Ensure the tag exists locally (`git tag v1.0.0` should show it).  
2. Check out that exact snapshot with `git checkout v1.0.0` (puts you in detached HEAD).  
3. Run your usual sanity checks—e.g. `pnpm install`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`, maybe `pnpm dev` for a quick manual click-through.

When you’re ready for the next iteration, just `git checkout main` (or whichever branch you’re continuing on) and continue normal development. The tag stays put as an immutable reference to that release, so you can always repeat the smoke test later by checking out the tag again.

## My request for Codex:
you mean  if i go dev into v2.0.0 
in the same branch another dev still clone v.1.0.0 that i waqs published right ?

Right. Branch history keeps moving forward as you develop toward v2.0.0, but the `v1.0.0` tag always points to the exact commit you tagged. So even if you push new commits on `001-mock-dashboard-app`, anyone can still fetch the repo (or run `git fetch --tags`), then `git checkout v1.0.0` to get that older state. Tags are immutable bookmarks—publishing new work on the same branch doesn’t affect them.
